text:
Philadelphia Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson is returning for the 2026 season after a Lisfranc injury ended his 2025 season.

Johnson was frustrated with the Eagles' offense in 2025, which he described as "predictable" before it ranked 24th in yards per game.

The Eagles have a new offensive coordinator and offensive line coach, implementing a new system that Johnson is eager to learn.

PHILADELPHIA − Lane Johnson couldn't stand the word. It ate at him early in the 2025 season. And it left a bitter taste in the mouth of the Eagles' right tackle when his season ended last Nov. 16 due to a Lisfranc injury.

That's why Johnson said he had already made up his mind to return for the 2026 season despite having so many reasons to hang up his cleats.

But first, let's start with the word "predictable," something Johnson uttered multiple times, unprompted, following the Eagles' 34-17 loss to the Giants last Oct. 9. It's also why Johnson is No. 5 in our countdown of the Eagles' eight most intriguing players heading into the start of training camp on July 28.

Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets

"I don’t know if we’re predictable, but it seems a lot harder than what it needs to be," Johnson said after that Thursday night debacle. "Maybe moving forward have a little bit more variety, hitting the perimeter some and doing a little bit more of that."

Johnson stopped talking to the media after that game. But the problem didn't go away. The Eagles' offense ranked 24th in the NFL in yards per game and 19th in scoring in 2025.

Still, the Eagles were 8-2 after that 16-9 win over the Lions. That came one week after they beat the Packers in Green Bay 10-7. That Packers game began a stretch where the Eagles scored 21 points or less in 8 of their final 10 games, including their playoff loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

After the season, offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo was fired and offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland decided not to return. Johnson called Stoutland's departure "a shocking ordeal." After all, Stoutland was the only offensive line coach that Johnson had during his 13 seasons with the Eagles.

And, oh yeah, Johnson's foot injury prevented him from returning for the playoff game against the 49ers.

Johnson could have easily called it a career, walked into the sunset knowing that he would be in the Hall of Fame soon enough. But Johnson said he never considered that. Not after the way last season went.

"I was just mad," Johnson said. "I thought I was having a really good season last year. Man, there was nobody more disappointed than me not being able to come in and play, to finish it out. I didn’t want to go out that way."

Still, it's going to be dramatically different for Johnson. There's a new offensive coordinator in Sean Mannion, who's installing an offense based on the Kyle Shanahan/Sean McVay model. And there's a new offensive line coach in Chris Kuper, hired by Mannion to install a new system and implement new blocking schemes.

Talking about teaching an old dog new tricks.

"I’ve watched this system ... from afar, and I’ve always envied wanting to be a part of it," Johnson said. "So here I am, after all these years, getting that chance. Not to say we’re going to be better, but there’s a lot to learn. I think we have the ability to be a lot more than what we were last year."

The new system will require the Eagles' offensive linemen to use their athleticism in running more outside zone instead of just overpowering defensive linemen and linebackers down the field.

That system with Stoutland also doubling as the run game coordinator worked well enough for the Eagles in their Super Bowl runs in 2022 and 2024. And really, during most of Nick Sirianni's tenure as head coach beginning in 2021.

Johnson, of course, has been one of the linchpins. He was selected to the Pro Bowl six times, and is one of only two Eagles on the team to have two Super Bowl rings. His importance is amplified by the Eagles' record when Johnson plays (94-41-1, .695 winning percentage) as opposed to when he doesn't (15-28, .349), including a 3-5 record last season.

Now that Johnson is fully healed, he said he has a lot more to give.

"A lot of guys trend down in their 30s," he said. "I feel like my career has been the opposite. My career started blossoming in my 30s. So last year, me being out of the game was kind of like, ‘Hey, if you don’t stay healthy, it’s going to be a glimpse of what it could become.’

"Like I said, I wanted to come back and finish on a strong note, and really say I really got everything out of myself."

If Johnson does that, the Eagles' offense in 2026 will be anything but predictable.

text:
COLLEGE PARK, Ga. (AP) — Jordin Canada made a layup at the buzzer and the Atlanta Dream bounced back after squandering a 22-point lead and losing star Angel Reese due to a knee injury, beating the Chicago Sky 93-91 on Sunday.

The victory was Atlanta’s seventh straight over Chicago.

After Allisha Gray hit two free throws with 9.5 seconds left, the Sky took a timeout to advance the ball to the front count. Sydney Taylor took the inbounds pass, worked around a high screen by Kamilla Cardoso and hit a deep, straight-away 3 to make it 91-all four seconds later.

Canada took a handoff from Brionna Jones on the right wing and darted to the hoop for the go-ahead basket.

Reese’s knee buckled when she came to a jump stop under the basket early in the fourth quarter and she fell to the ground as she missed the layup. She got up quickly, but went down again after a few seconds. Reese returned to the bench and the Dream ruled her out for the rest of the game.

Gray led the Dream (16-10) with 29 points, and Canada finished with 10 points, nine assists and three steals. Madina Okot had 14 points and four rebounds in 11 minutes. Jones grabbed 10 rebounds to go with six points in 15 minutes off the bench. The four-time All-Star missed the first 24 games while recovering from a knee injury before she played 15 minutes in a 111-92 win at Toronto on Friday.

Atlanta has won three straight and four of its last five following a five-game skid.

The Sky (9-17) had their two-game win streak snapped.

Azura Stevens led Chicago with 20 points and nine rebounds. Taylor scored 18 and Kamilla Cardoso added 15.

The Sky’s Skylar Diggins (knee) missed her sixth consecutive game.

Atlanta’s Te-Hina Paopao (leg) missed her second game in a row.

Atlanta beat the Sky 82-75 in Chicago on June 9.

Up next

Sky: Play Wednesday at New York.

Dream: Visit Dallas on Wednesday.

text:
Coming off a roller coaster of two games that took place on Friday and Saturday, the Washington Nationals are looking to win their series over the Athletics with a victory in the finale on Sunday.

But prior to first pitch, the team announced some roster moves that featured yet another injury to their pitching staff. Not only was left-handed pitcher PJ Poulin placed on the 15-day injured list with a left flexor strain, but left-handed pitcher Richard Lovelady was moved to the 60-day IL due to his left triceps strain. As part of those moves, the Nationals re-signed left-hander Matt Krook to a major league contract, and they activated him ahead of Sunday's game.

Matt Krook Now Set to Play Crucial Part of This Bullpen

Krook, who recently departed the organization after he opted to become a free agent instead of accepting an outright assignment to Triple-A Rochester after he was designated for assignment and cleared waivers, is now poised to have a much larger role in Washington based on this injury update.

With Lovelady now expected to miss a significant amount of time following his transfer to the 60-day injured list, and with Poulin getting diagnosed with a concerning injury of his own, Krook now has the chance to be a featured part of this bullpen.

That might scare some people based on the 14.11 career ERA he has across 16 MLB appearances. However, outside of the disastrous blowup Krook had against the New York Yankees when manager Blake Butera inserted him into a save situation, the lefty has thrown 2 1/3 scoreless innings for the Nationals with just one hit allowed and two strikeouts to two walks.

Washington needs much more of that going forward, especially now that injuries are starting to pile up for this relief staff that already was one of the worst in the majors at full strength.

PJ Poulin Could Miss Extended Time

This was not a good diagnosis when it comes to Poulin, as flexor strains have historically been a precursor to injuries that ultimately can lead to Tommy John surgeries or the new internal brace procedures.

The last time Poulin appeared in a game for the Nationals was on July 11 against the Yankees, so the fact that he was still dealing with something over the All-Star break that prevented him from appearing in the first two games of Washington's set against the Athletics is not a positive sign.

Hopefully some rest will prevent a long-term injury for Poulin when it comes to dealing with this flexor strain. But that also means the Nationals are likely to be without one of their most versatile and effective relievers for a while during the second half of the season.

text:
San Francisco Giants shortstop Willy Adames has admitted that a lingering back problem has affected his season, but he refuses to use the injury as an excuse for his struggles on the field.

Before Saturday night's game against the Seattle Mariners, Adames spoke honestly about his performance during the first half of the season. He acknowledged that he has not played at the level he expects, both offensively and defensively.

Adames enters Sunday's action slashing .230/.280.432 with a career-worst .712 OPS. He was also on pace to finish the season with a career-high 23 errors.

Willy Adames on His 2026 Season

Adames took a direct approach during a recent interview.

“You have to be really honest with yourself, and I know I haven’t been my best on both sides,” Adames told the San Francisco Chronicle's Susan Slusser (subscription required). “This year has been a rough year. Hopefully, it can change in the second half and I can be better on both sides, we can be better on both sides and finish the year we want.”

The Giants started the second half on a high note with a 7-0 victory over Seattle on Friday. Adames played a key role by hitting a grand slam. He stayed hot on Saturday, adding another home run, although San Francisco fell 4-3 to the Mariners.

The four-day All-Star break gave Adames time to rest after dealing with back problems for much of the season. While he won't blame it for the downturn in his performance — and an MRI has revealed no significant damage — it is presenting him with limitations.

Adames — who hit 30 home runs last season in spite of his .225 average — has to receive treatment to loosen the back up every day.

The daily recovery routine has limited the amount of defensive work he can do on the field. Instead of spending extra time practicing, Adames has to focus on managing his back and reducing the strain.

That has been especially disappointing because the Giants have veteran coach Ron Washington, who is widely respected for developing infielders. Adames would like to spend more time working with Washington, but repeated ground-ball drills and long sessions in a deep crouch are difficult because of his back.

As the Giants continue the second half of the 2026 season, Adames will hope improved health helps him return to the level of play the team expected when it signed him.

title: Three-Man Starting Battle In Bears' Pass Rush - Pro Football Rumors
description:
Last year, the Bears employed free agent addition Dayo Odeyingbo as a starter after signing him to a three-year, $48MM contract.
Starting 14 games in a contract year, Odeyingbo only totaled three sacks, though he created a decent amount of pressure, as evidenced by 17 quarterback hits.
In his first year in Chicago, Odeyingbo started eight games before suffering a torn Achilles tendon.
In 10 games, Booker delivered to some degree on the breakout promise, notching 4.5 sacks, five tackles for loss, and 12 quarterback hits.
So, the Bears have two players coming back from serious injuries and Booker, who impressed to some degree in his return from injury last year.
text:
The Bears finished 2025 with the seventh-fewest sacks in the league. Star pass rusher Montez Sweat led the team with 10.0 sacks, 13 tackles for loss, and 18 quarterback hits, but no other defensive end on the team reached even half his sack total. Chicago will be looking for someone to step up in 2026, and according to Courtney Cronin of ESPN, a three-man competition will play out over training camp to determine who will start across from Sweat.

Last year, the Bears employed free agent addition Dayo Odeyingbo as a starter after signing him to a three-year, $48MM contract. The team was counting on Odeyingbo to take a step forward after only amassing 16.5 sacks in four years with the Colts. To be fair, Odeyingbo didn’t start until his final year in Indianapolis. He showed strong progress leading up to that, improving from 0.5 sacks as a rookie to five in Year 2 then tallying eight in 2023. Starting 14 games in a contract year, Odeyingbo only totaled three sacks, though he created a decent amount of pressure, as evidenced by 17 quarterback hits.

In his first year in Chicago, Odeyingbo started eight games before suffering a torn Achilles tendon. He notched a sack, a tackle for loss, and two quarterback hits in his first game with the team, but over the next seven weeks, Odeyingbo only made one more tackle for loss and two more quarterback hits. Odeyingbo is expected to return to the field in training camp, but whenever he does, he’ll have to fend off two challengers for his starting position.

Before the 2025 season began, second-year end Austin Booker had been tabbed as a breakout candidate, but a knee injury in the preseason put him on injured reserve for the first eight weeks of the season. Booker’s first game back was the day Odeyingbo got hurt, allowing for a smooth transition for Booker into the starting lineup for the second half of the season. In 10 games, Booker delivered to some degree on the breakout promise, notching 4.5 sacks, five tackles for loss, and 12 quarterback hits.

The third man in this competition is second-year defender Shemar Turner. The Texas A&M-product debuted in the third week of the season as the Bears worked to shift him out from the more traditional interior role he played in College Station to the edge. The rookie second-rounder ended up splitting his time between the two positions in a rotational role off the bench but wasn’t able to produce much before tearing his ACL the week before Odeyingbo’s injury. Upon his return from injury, though, Chicago reportedly intends to continue working him in an edge role.

So, the Bears have two players coming back from serious injuries and Booker, who impressed to some degree in his return from injury last year. The team didn’t make any moves in the draft or free agency to supplement the group, so it seems clear they feel confident moving forward with the group they have. On that note, though, Cronin believes that, if Odeyingbo’s return in camp doesn’t inspire confidence that he’ll be able to effectively contribute this year, Chicago may become a potential destination for one of several veteran free agent pass rushers on the market today.

text:
Angel Reese’s eventful weekend ended with an injury and one of her worst performances of the season.

The Atlanta Dream star left Sunday afternoon’s game against her former team, the Chicago Sky, after her left leg appeared to give out as she attempted a layup early in the fourth quarter.

ANGEL REESE THANKS WNBA FOR SUSPENDING SANDY BRONDELLO, FRAMES ‘PROTECTED SPECIES’ COMMENT AS DISCRIMINATION

Reese fell to the floor after missing the shot, briefly got back to her feet and then went down again. She eventually returned to Atlanta’s bench, but the Dream ruled her out for the remainder of the game with a left leg injury.

But Reese wasn’t playing particularly well before leaving the game.

And that's actually putting it kindly.

The 24-year-old finished with eight points and five rebounds in 20 minutes. She shot an abysmal 3-of-13 from the field, missed her only three-point attempt and committed three turnovers. She finished with a minus-7 rating in Atlanta’s 93-91 victory. Her minus-7 was the worst mark among Dream players, and she committed three fouls.

Not good.

In addition, Reese grabbed just one defensive rebound. Four of her five boards came on the offensive end, including two "mebounds" where she grabs her own rebound after missing a short shot.

That’s become a familiar part of the Angel Reese experience.

ANGEL REESE GIVES ATLANTA DREAM REBOUNDS AND ATTENTION, BUT HER OFFENSE IS STILL A PROBLEM

She is unquestionably one of the best rebounders in women’s basketball. She also regularly pads those totals by collecting misses around the basket, including her own.

On Sunday, even that wasn’t enough to make the box score look respectable.

Reese entered the game averaging 15.7 points and a league-leading 11.8 rebounds per contest. She had recorded 23 points and 12 rebounds against Toronto on Friday, her league-leading 17th double-double of the season.

She followed that performance by missing 10 of 13 shots against the team that traded her during the offseason.

The rough outing wasn’t caused by the injury, either.

Reese had already logged 20 minutes before getting hurt 14 seconds into the fourth.

Again, the injury is unfortunate. There’s nothing funny about a player getting hurt, and the hope is that Reese avoided anything serious.

After the game, Dream head coach Karl Smesko said Reese was in "great spirits celebrating with her teammates."

According to WNBA reporter Wilton Jackson, Smesko noted that Reese "wanted to go out there and keep playing" but that he "didn't feel comfortable with it because she looked like she was in a lot of pain."

Despite the injury, it's hard to look past just how bad Reese was prior to getting hurt.

Fortunately for the All-Star forward, her teammates bailed her out.

Atlanta led by as many as 22 points before allowing Chicago to erase the deficit. The Dream led by one point when Reese exited.

Atlanta guard Jordin Canada made a game-winning layup as time expired and the Dream escaped with a 93-91 victory over the 9-17 Sky.

The Dream improved to 16-10 and Reese is now 2-0 against the Sky since Atlanta acquired her for two first-round draft picks in April.

Still, this wasn’t exactly the revenge performance Reese probably envisioned against her former team.

CAITLIN CLARK'S FORMER TEAMMATE CALLS OUT WNBA FOR SUSPENDING TEMPO HEAD COACH OVER 'PROTECTED SPECIES' REMARK

She had more missed shots (10) than either points (8) or rebounds (5). She also turned the ball over three times and committed three fouls before hurting her leg.

The good news for Atlanta is that they don't play again until July 29, which gives Reese plenty of time to recover. The bad news is that the WNBA All-Star Game is on July 25 and the league certainly prefers that Reese plays in that game.

Say what you will about Reese, but she's arguably the second-biggest draw in the league after Caitlin Clark. Despite this poor performance, there's no question Reese adds intrigue to the All-Star Game.

Hopefully, she recovers in time to play.

text:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo said he’s “perfectly fine” after a perilous landing on his freshly healed right leg following an attempted backflip on the Fanatics Fest stage in New York.

A clip of the second-year ball carrier awkwardly falling and landing dangerously after attempting the flip went viral Saturday night. On Sunday, Skattebo, speaking at another Fanatics Fest event, assured fans that he was OK.

“I’m gonna address the elephant,” he said while sitting next to Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart. “I will not hurt myself before the season.”

Before attempting the flip on Saturday, Skattebo pulled up his pants to show his right leg, where he suffered a fractured fibula, ruptured deltoid ligament and dislocated ankle in a Week 8 injury that ended his rookie season. He said the floor was bouncy and he did not anticipate how much it would give, which led to the treacherous landing.

Dart joked it was “the most explosive I’ve seen Skatt.”

While Dart might have been impressed, the clip likely raised the blood pressures of Giants fans and coaches who are hoping to have Skattebo back on the field this year.

The former Arizona State standout’s rookie season was limited to just eight games due to injuries. He tallied 410 rushing yards and five touchdowns along with 207 receiving yards and two touchdowns in 2025 before suffering the season-ending injury against the Philadelphia Eagles.

This isn’t the first time Skattebo’s off-field activities have drawn scrutiny.

Last November, he was the subject of criticism for appearing on “Monday Night Raw” with some of his teammates shortly after the Week 8 injury.

Skattebo defended that appearance, saying: “I’m not able to play football and have the fun I’ve been having my whole life, so I am doing things outside the box trying to find stuff to keep me happy.”

In March, he apologized for “a tasteless joke” he made on a podcast when he suggested that chronic traumatic encephalopathy, the degenerative brain disease known as CTE, was not real.

On Sunday, he said he had no plans to change his behavior.

“I’m just gonna keep being me, “ Skattebo said. “If they wanna say I’m braindead and I don’t have no brain, then who cares? F— it.”

text:
ATLANTA (AP) — Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese left Sunday’s victory over Chicago with a left leg injury.

Reese’s knee buckled when she came to a jump stop under the basket early in the fourth quarter and she fell to the ground as she missed the layup. She got up quickly, but went down again after a few seconds.

Reese returned to the bench and the Dream ruled her out for the rest of the game. The Dream did not provide an update on Reese after the team’s 93-91 win over the Sky.

“It’s hard because we’re in the timeout. It seemed like a really long timeout and there wasn’t a lot being said because we were all just looking at Angel,” Dream coach Karl Smesko said. “And when I was looking at her, it seemed like she was in a lot of pain, and she wanted to go out there and and keep playing because she’s competitive and she wants to win the game. I just didn’t feel comfortable with it because she looked like she was in a lot of pain.”

Reese was named a WNBA All-Star in her first season with the Dream, leading the league with 11.8 rebounds and 14 double-doubles. She’s averaging 14.9 points.

text:
The San Francisco 49ers are a different team with George Kittle on the field. Anyone who has watched them play a single game with a healthy Kittle knows that.

That’s why the 2026 season has such a cloud over it to begin with, thanks to the uncertainty around Kittle’s recovery from a torn Achilles tendon suffered in the NFC Wild Card Round win over the Philadelphia Eagles.

Advertisement

San Jose Mercury News NFL reporter Cam Inman believes the 49ers are in a critical “bind” at tight end as they wait to see what happens with Kittle.

“(Kittle’s recovery) is the 49ers’ biggest question, and until he is cleared, they are in a bind, entering training camp with essentially the same options from last season,” Inman wrote on July 19. “Less than eight months after his right Achilles ruptured in a wild-card playoff win at Philadelphia, Kittle can take aim at playing in the 49ers’ season opener against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia. But if he opens camp on the (PUP) list and remains there the opening four games, no one would blame the 49ers for protecting their franchise’s most proficient tight end ever.”

To make matters worse, the 49ers didn’t draft a tight end in 2026 and didn’t sign a veteran free agent — at least not yet, anyway.

Pair of 49ers Superstars Coming Off Serious Injuries

Getting a player on Bleacher Report’s “10 Key Injuries to Monitor” before any season is less than ideal. Getting 2 of them on there might be considered an emergency.

Advertisement

That’s where the San Francisco 49ers sit headed into 2026, with 2 of their 3 most important players coming off devastating, season-ending injuries, with NFL All-Pro Kittle and NFL All-Pro edge rusher Nick Bosa (torn ACL).

B/R’s Brad Gagnon wrote the 2 injuries could “deeply impact how the upcoming season plays out” — and he couldn’t be more right.

“San Francisco really needs a healthy season — something it seemingly has never experienced in franchise history,” Gagnon wrote on July 1. “Kittle’s presence is critical for that offense, as he’s Brock Purdy‘s experienced and reliable safety valve … they’ll want to count on Bosa to play a major role as soon as possible. Keep in mind that this defense produced a league-low 20 sacks last season, and 2025 first-round edge Mykel Williams is also rehabbing a November ACL tear. ”

49ers Paying Massive Money for George Kittle

The 49ers are paying through the teeth for Kittle in 2026.

Advertisement

Kittle signed a 4-year, $76.4 million contract extension in April 2025, and it remains the biggest contract signed by a tight end in NFL history. The 49ers are working with a manageable cap hit of $14.1 million for Kittle in 2026, but that’s still a lot of money to pay someone who might not play.

Backup tight end Jake Tonges showed he was somewhat competent in 2025 with career highs of 34 receptions for 293 yards and 5 touchdowns and signed a 2-year, $8 million contract extension this offseason.

Kittle, a 7-time Pro Bowler and 5-time NFL All-Pro, is 3rd in franchise history with 8,008 receiving yards and cracked the NFL’s Top 10 career receiving list for tight ends in 2025 with 57 receptions for 628 yards and 7 touchdowns in just 11 games.

With 1 or 2 more standout seasons, Kittle could very well cement his place in the Pro Football Hall of Fame once his career is over.

text:
As Shohei Ohtani continues to deal with a lingering knee injury, the Dodgers have opted to keep him out of the pitching rotation for his next scheduled start, which was originally set for Wednesday, July 22. Manager Dave Roberts told reporters Sunday that it may be a while until Ohtani returns to his duties as a pitcher, as L.A. aims to prioritize caution with its two-way superstar.

“His knee, we just want to continue to give it the best chance to kind of get into a good spot. And as he said, as we feel, it’s the pitching and the torque of landing on that leg that kind of gets it upset,” Robert explained, via the NY Post.

Ohtani felt discomfort in his knee while playing catch over the weekend. That development came after Ohtani was scratched from his final start before the All-Star break, and sat out the Midsummer Classic entirely in order to rest the knee. Now, as the injury lingers, the Dodgers don’t have a timeline for when the 32-year-old will be back on the mound during the second half of the season.

“It’s not going to be a day-to-day thing,” Roberts said. “The first step is getting him into a spot where he feels like, and we feel like, he can pitch and not regress. At that point in time, we can kind of read and react. I just can’t even answer [when that might be] right now.”

Keeping Ohtani healthy, or at least as healthy as he can be, is crucial for the Dodgers. So, while it’s unfortunate that he won’t be part of the team’s rotation for the time being, it’s undoubtedly the right call. Los Angeles already sits 12 games ahead of the second-place Diamondbacks in the NL West. The team is currently tracking to be the No. 1 seed in the National League, and is effectively a lock for the postseason.

After all, the Dodgers are vying to complete the first World Series three-peat since the Yankees did it from 1998 to 2000. Having their best player at full strength in the playoffs will be critical towards achieving that goal.

With Blake Snell currently on his way back from injury—having recently been sent out on a rehab assignment—letting Ohtani get back to full strength is a wise move. When Snell is back, he can assume Ohtani’s vacant rotation spot, and Tyler Glasnow should be ready to rejoin the mix at some point in August, too. They could also look to make a splash at the trade deadline in order to bring in another arm, as the team boasts a loaded farm system in addition to its league-best MLB roster.

There are plenty of ways the Dodgers can navigate Ohtani’s absence from the mound, especially considering their success in the first half of the season, which has them comfortably in position to reach the postseason. The team wants to continue deploying a six-man rotation, and bullpen games are certainly in the cards in the meantime as they await Snell’s return.

Ohtani will continue to serve as the Dodgers’ leadoff hitter and DH even while he’s unavailable to pitch. Although his arm will be out of commission for a while, the team will still get his invaluable production atop the batting order. And come October, when the team gears up for another run to the World Series, Ohtani’s knee will (hopefully) be at a point where he’s able to re-take the mound. Roberts indicated that Ohtani “could” pitch presently, though the risk of further aggravating his injury outweighs the benefits of having him pitching every six or seven days. He did make clear when speaking to reporters Sunday, however, that the team is still expecting Ohtani to pitch again in 2026.

text:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo said he is "perfectly fine" after failing to land a backflip and appearing to land awkwardly on his surgically repaired right ankle during an appearance at Fanatics Fest on Saturday.

Video of Skattebo attempting his trademark backflip went viral after he fell to the ground while trying to land the flip. Addressing the "elephant in the room" at another Fanatics Fest appearance Sunday, Skattebo said he is good following the fall and promised to "not hurt myself before the season." He blamed the botched flip on the "bouncy" floors.

Skattebo's rookie season was cut short after suffering an open tibia fracture and right ankle dislocation in a gruesome-looking injury during a Week 8 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. He missed the rest of the season but has made significant progress in his recovery and is on track to be a full participant in Giants training camp next month.

It's not the first time Skattebo has attempted a backflip in recent weeks. He was seen sticking the landing on the flip after hitting a home run during a celebrity softball game May 30. New Giants coach John Harbaugh joked last month that he told the running back "no backflips" at minicamp.

Despite the reaction to his attempted flip on social media, Skattebo promised he is not going to change who he is.

"I'm just going to keep being me, and if they want to say I'm brain-dead, and I don't have no brain, then who cares, f--- it," he said.

text:
Three different players made at least four starts and played at least 200 snaps at left tackle for the Bears last year.

Braxton Jones opened the year as the starter, but was benched in Week 4 after a rough start and later landed on injured reserve. Second-year UDFA Theo Benedet took over on the blind side for seven games before being supplanted by 2025 second-round pick Ozzy Trapilo. He started the next six games, sat in Week 18 due to injury (with Benedet replacing him), and suffered a season-ending torn patellar tendon in the wild card round. The Bears then called on Joe Thuney to play left tackle in their divisional round loss to the Rams.

Chicago drafted Trapilo last year in the hopes he could become their long-term left tackle. But he is expected to be sidelined for most, if not all, of 2026. So, the Bears retained Jones on a one-year, $5MM, setting him as their presumptive starter for the upcoming season. The 27-year-old took all of the team’s first-team reps in spring practices, per ESPN’s Courtney Cronin, though free agent signing Jedrick Wills and Kiran Amegadjie will still push for the starting job.

Jones attributed last year’s struggles in part to his 2024 ankle injury and acknowledged the mental difficulties of coming back from major surgery.

“I just don’t think I was at my best with my injury, and mentally it can be a lot,” Jones said. “But I’m grateful for that, to be able to look back and see that and realize that I was right there, I just needed to trust what I was in.”

title: McCorkle: The Best (And Worst) Scenarios For Every Steelers Rookie
description:
But that won’t stop me from taking another crack at projecting the ceiling and floor for every Steelers rookie.
He never earns a full-time starting job, and has to treat his rookie season as a learning experience.
Worst-Case Scenario: He not only fails to make the team, but they can’t find a spot for him on the practice squad.
Worst-Case Scenario: Tough roster decisions force Spears-Jennings to the practice squad in favor of Sebastian Castro and Darnell Savage.
He will be a core four-unit special teamer during his rookie season and end with 10 or more ST tackles.
text:
NFL teams don’t have the luxury of waiting three years for first-round picks to develop anymore. Whether it’s fair or not, rookies are expected to contribute almost immediately, especially on teams expecting to win now like the Steelers.

Predicting the outcome of rookie seasons can be tough. Just look at my guesses last May. Let’s just say my crystal ball was a little bit foggy that day. But that won’t stop me from taking another crack at projecting the ceiling and floor for every Steelers rookie.

R1:21 – OT Max Iheanachor

Best-Case Scenario:

He wins the week-one starting job in training camp over Dylan Cook and proves that the “raw” label he was stuck with in the draft process was lazy analysis. In the process, he stabilizes a right side of the offensive line that many view as lacking entering the season, and helps the heavily-invested O-line finally turn into a top unit.

Worst-Case Scenario:

The knocks against him turn out to be true, and he needs time to adjust to the speed and technical requirements of the NFL game. In the few opportunities he gets due to injury, he displays many of the same issues that plagued Broderick Jones at his worst points over the last couple years. He never earns a full-time starting job, and has to treat his rookie season as a learning experience.

My Prediction:

Dylan Cook will exit camp as the starter, but with a short leash. The extra practice time before being thrown into the deep end will pay off for Iheanachor, and he will hit the ground running with a very impressive debut. By the end of the season, he will look like an early success story for the Steelers with sky-high expectations for the 2027 offensive line.

R2:47 – WR Germie Bernard

Best-Case Scenario:

He wins the competition against Roman Wilson in training camp and proves to be a bargain from the second round of the draft. Playing more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps, he continues breaking the rookie stigma with Aaron Rodgers (like Christian Watson did in 2022) and hauls in 35 passes for 550 yards and a few touchdowns. His performance lands him on the fast track to being WR2 for the Steelers and makes one of Michael Pittman Jr. or DK Metcalf expendable.

Worst-Case Scenario:

Rodgers and Bernard can’t get on the same page, and he becomes this year’s version of 2025 Roman Wilson while Wilson himself fills the WR3 role. He flashes in the few opportunities he gets, but Rodgers doesn’t have the patience in his final NFL season for rookie mistakes.

My Prediction:

Bernard and Wilson exit camp on even footing, but Bernard slowly pulls ahead as the clear No. 3 option as the season wears on. Rodgers finds his groove with Bernard in the second half of the season, and the rookie catches 20 passes over the final month to set up maximum hype for 2027. I expect a 400-yard season out of him.

R3:76 – QB Drew Allar

Best-Case Scenario:

He flashes in the preseason, stays healthy, and absorbs all he can from Aaron Rodgers.

Worst-Case Scenario:

Injuries strike and Allar is forced into action before he’s ready, throwing a wrench in the development program, and forcing him back to old habits that set him back.

My Prediction:

His preseason performance will be largely unimpressive, other than one or two deep bombs that give everybody hope for the future.

R3:85 – CB Daylen Everette

Best-Case Scenario:

He wins the top backup job over Asante Samuel Jr., which results in him starting a few games due to injury. His experience against top college competition proves useful as he posts a Joey Porter Jr.-like performance against at least one top receiver as a rookie.

Worst-Case Scenario:

He spends the season as a reserve defender and special teamer learning.

My Prediction:

Due to his solid fundamentals and tackling, he supplants Samuel and makes him expendable at the trade deadline. He plays about 25 percent of the defensive snaps for the season, including some opportunities in the slot, and sets up a big second year.

R3:96 – OG Gennings Dunker

Best-Case Scenario:

Transitioning from tackle to guard proves easier than expected and he puts himself in position to earn the starting right guard job at the first sign of failure from Spencer Anderson or Brock Hoffman. His play strength and nasty demeanor flash over the second half of the season and he helps power one of Pittsburgh’s best rushing offenses in years.

Worst-Case Scenario:

His technique needs work, and he spends his entire rookie season as a reserve offensive lineman, and maybe not even the first one off the bench in case of injury.

My Prediction:

Dunker doesn’t start a single game in 2026 as he learns the ins and outs of playing a new position in the NFL.

R4:121 – WR/KR Kaden Wetjen

Best-Case Scenario:

He breaks Pittsburgh’s TD drought in the kick return game and proves his fourth-round selection wasn’t a reach. He even gets involved on offense in a gadget role with clear upside there in the future.

Worst-Case Scenario:

The return game doesn’t improve any from recent years and the draft “reach” noise grows louder. The few experiments they attempt on offense with him flop, and his only value is as a return specialist.

My Prediction:

Wetjen won’t break any return touchdowns, but the average yards per return will increase from previous years. Getting him involved on offense will be tough with too many other mouths to feed in the passing game.

R5:169 – FB/TE Riley Nowakowski

Best-Case Scenario:

Nowakowski continues his clutch playmaking from Indiana and provides a new dimension to the offense as a hybrid fullback making plays out of the backfield. He helps pave the way for Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle and becomes a reliable lead blocker in short-yardage situations.

Worst-Case Scenario:

He doesn’t make the roster with Rodgers’ old friend Robert Tonyan creating a math problem in the TE room.

My Prediction:

Nowakowski makes the roster and plays about 15 percent of the team’s offensive snaps. When he’s on the field, his contributions become noticeable, and he catches a critical touchdown at some point during the season.

R6:210 – DL Gabriel Rubio

Best-Case Scenario:

He makes the roster, but mostly as a game day inactive all season.

Worst-Case Scenario:

He not only fails to make the team, but they can’t find a spot for him on the practice squad.

My Prediction:

Rubio wasn’t a very well-known prospect, so he can safely clear waivers and make it to the practice squad. The team may call him up as a game day elevation once or twice as a run stuffer if injuries strike.

R7:224 – S Robert Spears-Jennings

Best-Case Scenario:

His speed and special teams ability earn him a spot on the 53-man roster, where he gets to play about 15 percent of the team’s defensive snaps at safety due to injuries.

Worst-Case Scenario:

Tough roster decisions force Spears-Jennings to the practice squad in favor of Sebastian Castro and Darnell Savage.

My Prediction:

Spears-Jennings speed will turn a lot of heads at training camp, as it did throughout the spring, and the coaching staff won’t be able to justify cutting him. He will be a core four-unit special teamer during his rookie season and end with 10 or more ST tackles.

R7:230 – RB Eli Heidenreich

Best-Case Scenario:

He not only makes the roster, but he carves out a niche role on offense with his receiving skills. Mike McCarthy and Brian Angelichio really do “open up the playbook,” as they suggested after drafting him, and he gets 10 touches for 100 yards and a TD while becoming a key special teams contributor.

title: England World Cup player ratings: Historic Bellingham, Rice's struggles, Kane frustration
authors: Jack Pitt-Brooke, Adam Crafton and Reuben Pinder, Tim Spiers
description:
So, how did his World Cup squad perform?
C+ Midfielders Declan Rice: Came into this World Cup on a high, having won the Premier League with Arsenal, and being named England vice-captain.
B+ Morgan Rogers: Before the World Cup, he was battling with Bellingham for a starting role.
Helped turn the Norway game with his energy in the middle, including the shot Bellingham converted for the winner.
C Harry Kane: Matched his tally of six goals from the 2018 World Cup, putting him clear as England’s greatest tournament goalscorer.
text:
England have arrived home after the World Cup, fresh from recording their best finish at the tournament since 1966, but will hold a lingering sense of regret.

They beat France in Saturday’s third-placed play-off, but the semi-final defeat against Argentina goes down as a glorious missed opportunity. Head coach Thomas Tuchel will be under scrutiny when England return to international action in September in the UEFA Nations League.

So, how did his World Cup squad perform?

Goalkeepers

Jordan Pickford: His third World Cup in goal for England will always be remembered for the Azteca, where his crucial saves kept England in the game, he punched perfectly and ran down the clock at the end. It was a moment as memorable as his famous save from Carlos Bacca in Moscow eight years ago. Pickford has been an integral player through this England era, but he will know he was not perfect at this tournament. He was beaten at his near post by Brian Cipenga in the last 32, a goal that would be remembered forever had England not turned it around.

Against Norway, he misjudged Andreas Schjelderup’s cross, putting England in a difficult position. Then in the semi-final, Pickford was beaten by Enzo Fernandez from distance, the goal that precipitated England’s exit. The question as England embark on their next cycle is whether there is true competition for him. B-

Dean Henderson: Came in cold for the France game and England could easily have conceded more than four goals, with Henderson making some fine saves. Has his strengths but will never be as good with his feet as Pickford. B-

James Trafford: The third-choice goalkeeper did not get on the field. N/A

Defenders

John Stones: Tuchel had spent his whole tenure planning to build around Stones, knowing that the 32-year-old offers him things that no other English centre-back can. So it was a surprise when he was benched after the Croatia game and did not feature again until the knockouts.

Stones’ experience was vital in the Azteca rearguard, earning him a return to the starting XI. The way he closed down Alexander Sorloth in Miami kept England alive in the quarter-final when they were wobbling. If this is his last tournament — he insisted before the third-place play-off he wanted to keep going — it was a reminder that he is probably England’s finest centre-back of the modern era. B+

Marc Guehi: Came off the bench for the opening game against Croatia and then played every subsequent minute (of the competitive games), keeping his place at centre-back even when Stones returned. Was important to impressive defensive performances against Norway and Mexico, always maintaining his calm presence in difficult moments. B

Ezri Konsa: One of Tuchel’s most dependable players at this World Cup. He started the first five games at centre-back, but was fortunate to avoid conceding a penalty at the end of the Ghana game in Boston. But he did a heroic shift out on the right during the Mexico City rearguard, and then kept his spot at right-back against Norway. Like Guehi, he was integral to England grinding their way to the semi-final. And while his introduction against Argentina was a tactical misstep, that was not his fault. B

Trevoh Chalobah: Only appeared for a few minutes at the very end of the game against France. N/A

Djed Spence: One of the surprises in Tuchel’s squad but one of the more impressive performers, responding well to his coach’s pointed messaging. He started four games — three on the left, one on the right — but was more useful as an impact sub, coming on in the second half and using his speed to change the tempo of the game. Against Croatia, he was incisive, setting up England on the break.

At left wing-back in Mexico, he was perfect. And then, against Norway, he helped turn the tie with his surging runs and should have won a penalty too. (He finally earned a penalty against France.) His tackle against Giuliano Simeone would have been one of the moments of the tournament, if the rest of the game had gone differently. B+

Jarell Quansah: Came to the World Cup as a centre-back, but when Tino Livramento went home before it started, Tuchel said Quansah was now seen as a right-back. So he started there against Panama, before turning his ankle after an hour. He then came back into the starting XI away at Mexico and was doing well before getting sent off for a rash tackle that put England under severe pressure and earned him a two-game ban. C+

Nico O’Reilly: Left-back was a problem position for England coming into the tournament but O’Reilly established himself as first choice, starting five of England’s seven ‘competitive’ games there. The left side did not always click as intended but he worked hard going forward, sometimes coming inside and making attacking runs from midfield. Unfortunate in the opposition box, hitting the woodwork twice, but overall did well given that he only made his England debut last November. B

Reece James: A strange tournament. He arrived after recovering from a hamstring injury that kept him out for two months at the end of the season. He played England’s first two games here and then picked up another injury. He returned to play an important role in midfield against Norway, helping stem the flow, before returning to right-back for the Argentina game. But after so much time in and out of the team, he looked far from his best. C+

Midfielders

Declan Rice: Came into this World Cup on a high, having won the Premier League with Arsenal, and being named England vice-captain. But this season took more out of him than many realised. He never looked himself, despite starting seven games, and was withdrawn early against Croatia and Norway. He was unfortunate to pick up a stomach bug on top of the neural pain he was managing, but his uncharacteristic performances — not for lack of effort — underlined the extent to which England had no real replacement for him. C+

Elliot Anderson: It feels remarkable that Anderson only made his senior England debut last September. Had a huge midfield role given Rice’s struggles but coped fantastically, setting the tempo for England in the middle of the pitch and driving them forward. Never more so than for the first hour of the Argentina game, where he had to be perfect after picking up an unfortunate booking. Will be an England starter in the middle of the pitch for years to come. A

Jordan Henderson: Only played a few minutes, helping to close out the win over Panama. Still an important member of the squad, invaluable behind the scenes, setting standards and trying to keep everyone together. His return to the England camp after surgery on the wrist he broke during celebrations at the Azteca was further proof of his commitment. B

Jude Bellingham: England’s best player and one of the very best at the tournament. Answered all the questions about his attitude, team ethic and role with a series of brilliant performances. More than a No 10, he played as a box-to-box midfielder and a devastating striker simultaneously, ending up with seven goals, the most scored by any England player at a World Cup. Showcased athleticism scoring against Croatia, intelligence against Panama, ruthlessness with the double at the Azteca and then relentlessness with two against Norway. A+

Kobbie Mainoo: Unfortunate to pick up a back injury before the France game, meaning that he did not play one single minute. N/A

Eberechi Eze: Did not get to start a game until the third-place play-off, but made four substitute appearances before then. Had some nice touches along the way, especially against France, and was important in the win over Norway. But for all his technical tidiness, he rarely looked like he could quite make the difference that England needed. He is simply less dynamic than the alternatives for the ‘No 10’ role — Bellingham and Morgan Rogers — and not as quick as the wide-left options Anthony Gordon and Marcus Rashford. C

Forwards

Anthony Gordon: The best attacking player not called Harry Kane or Bellingham. Won the battle with Rashford to start on the left, but after a quiet two games, he lost it again. Two assists for Kane against DR Congo were a turning point. He then ran himself into the ground in Mexico and produced England’s only goal in the semi-final. Under different circumstances, it would have been one of the most important goals in English history. B+

Morgan Rogers: Before the World Cup, he was battling with Bellingham for a starting role. He ended up playing a bit-part role, but he was always lively when called upon. Started in midfield against Panama, but struggled to make a big impact. Helped turn the Norway game with his energy in the middle, including the shot Bellingham converted for the winner. Was rewarded for his efforts with a starting spot on the right against Argentina, and set up Gordon’s goal. B

Noni Madueke: Bukayo Saka’s injury problems meant that he played more than expected, starting four of the seven ‘competitive games’. Twice he lost his place to Saka, and then twice he came back in. Was always a willing runner and a good outlet when England needed to get up the pitch, staying high and wide as Tuchel wanted, attacking the space in behind. But he never got it right with his technical execution. Very few of Madueke’s crosses ever turned into chances, and his struggles against Norway meant he did not even get on the pitch in the semi-final. C

Bukayo Saka: His fitness was one of the stories of the campaign, as he struggled to shake off an Achilles issue that had troubled him during the club season. He had some good moments, not least his cross for the first goal in the Azteca. But he clearly struggled to go for the whole 90 minutes and it was telling that Tuchel did not bring him on against Argentina when England needed to change the energy. He then scored a hat-trick against France and went the full 90 minutes, suggesting that he may have had enough in his legs to make a difference. C+

Marcus Rashford: One of Tuchel’s big projects since he took the job, so much work was invested into trying to get Rashford performing here at his top level. But apart from his goal from the bench against Croatia, he did not offer enough. His final-third execution was off, and he didn’t contribute nearly as much without the ball as Gordon. So he lost his place after getting hooked against DR Congo and was not involved at all against Mexico and Norway. Only got a few desperate minutes against Argentina before returning with another dangerous first-half display on Saturday. C

Harry Kane: Matched his tally of six goals from the 2018 World Cup, putting him clear as England’s greatest tournament goalscorer. His performance in the DR Congo game in Atlanta will go down as one of his best, rescuing England from an embarrassing early exit with two goals, the second of which was a brilliant strike. But the frustrating thing, given how well he started, is that he faded after that. He scored a penalty in Mexico City but could not influence the Norway or Argentina games. And was left, not for the first time, frustrated by his inability to turn the very biggest games his way. A-

Ivan Toney: Only had a few minutes against Argentina to make an impact having not been called on otherwise during the tournament’s important stages. Given a start against France but failed to take the chance as he was overshadowed by the other attacking talent on the pitch. N/A

The New York Giants are optimistic heading into the 2026 campaign, and it’s not too hard to see why. Veteran head coach John Harbaugh is taking over a team led by a dynamic young core group on both sides of the ball, and while several of these guys are recovering from injuries, there’s reason to believe this team can take a serious step forward this upcoming season.

One player who is recovering from a serious ailment is running back Cam Skattebo, as he suffered a fractured tibia, among several other injuries, shortly after earning a starting job on offense last year. Skattebo has since been working his way back to full health, but in the wake of a video popping up on social media showing him doing a backflip at Fanatics Fest on Saturday, fans have quickly taken aim at him.

Giants Fans Won’t Love Cam Skattebo’s Latest Actions

While everyone was paying attention to the arrival of quarterback Jaxson Dart last year, the Giants also selected Skattebo in the 2025 NFL Draft with a fourth-round pick. After starting the year as a backup, Skattebo quickly became the team’s starter at the running back position, as he racked up 410 yards and five touchdowns on 101 carries in eight games, while also catching 24 passes for 207 yards and two more scores.

As noted above, though, Skattebo suffered a serious leg injury against the Philadelphia Eagles that brought a premature end to his season. Considering all the promise Skattebo was showcasing, losing him certainly hurt, but beyond that, there were questions about his availability for the start of the 2026 campaign.

Skattebo has been progressing well throughout the offseason, so much so that he was confident enough to do a backflip at Fanatics Fest over the weekend. As if that wasn’t bad enough, the Giants rusher didn’t exactly stick the landing, as he fell backwards, making an already concerning incident even worse. Unsurprisingly, it didn’t take long for fans to address Skattebo’s poor decision on social media.

“I can’t even imagine John Harbaugh’s reaction to seeing this LOL,” one fan said in response to the clip.

“Any reason why Cam Skattebo appears to be trying to end his own career?” another wondered.

“It’s early, but Cam Skattebo might be the dumbest NFL player of all time,” read another post alongside this video.

Giants Hoping Cam Skattebo Will Be Ready for Week 1

Skattebo certainly is a one-of-a-kind guy, and while that makes him endearing to fans in some ways, it’s also creating problems for the Giants. Realistically, seeing Skattebo do a backflip on his recently repaired leg is the last thing the team needs, but that just doesn’t register for him. Sure, he avoided catastrophe here, but who’s to say that will be the case the next time he does something reckless?

All eyes are going to be on Skattebo once training camp gets underway later this month to see what his level of participation is as he continues to work his way back to full health. In order for New York’s offense to operate at the highest level possible, it needs Skattebo on the field, which is why he has received so much flak for this hair-brained move.

The Detroit Lions EDGE position opposite Aidan Hutchinson has been a source of consternation for years - mainly due to injuries. Could a diamond in the rough emerge in the 2026 season?

The following are medical recaps of two EDGE players who could make a surprise impact. For more EDGE contenders including Ahmed Hassanein, visit Lions 2026 Training Camp Medical Preview: EDGE.

Payton Turner (27)

Medical concern level: 8/10

There were major concerns coming out of last season as he missed the entire year with a rib fracture. He also has missed the bulk of earlier seasons with toe surgery, shoulder, ankle, and chest. Prior to the NFL, he had a significant foot injury as well as an ACL tear.

So far this offseason, he’s been healthy, which drops his concern level down from the initial maxed-out 10/10. It’s quite possible he could have played some last season, but was shut down for other reasons.

OUTLOOK: Turner is like the younger version of the equally-unreliable Marcus Davenport. The Lions hope things work out better this time around. If he can stay healthy, Turner could be a very valuable part of the EDGE rotation.

Anthony Lucas (21)

Medical concern level: 2/10

This UDFA had ankle surgery in 2024, but has proof of recovery since. He is by far the youngest in the EDGE group, which is a big plus.

OUTLOOK: The Lions really could use someone to emerge from the rough. Lucas only had three sacks in college, but could have untapped potential because of his youth.

text:
CLEVELAND, OHIO (TheOBR.com) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans!

THE DAILY BLOVIATION

We're in the home stretch of the dead news period for the NFL and the Cleveland Browns, and starting to move into sites doing things like position-by-position camp previews and such. It's all the same stuff year after year, as media outlets limp through the downtime before players show up for training camp.

The rookies will show up first around mid-week, but there are no scheduled media availabilities for the team, so what you're going to get are photos of rookies walking into the Berea facility from the team's official site and not much else until the veterans show up in less than ten days.

There's no real news to talk about because, fortunately, the team has avoided any major off-field entanglements, so what a lot of sites wind up doing is writing about people writing about the Browns. I have a big white space on this Google Doc that I'm working on, so I guess I'll do the same.

I brought a couple of those types of stories with me. For instance, one is Warren Sharp putting out his 2026 front seven rankings, where he said something nice about the Browns, placing them at sixth in the league despite the loss of Myles Garrett. That's behind the Texans, Eagles, Rams, Broncos, and Seahawks, but ahead of the Steelers, the 49ers, and 27 other teams who would very much like to swap rooms with us. Top six in the league is top six in the league, regardless of who's doing the ranking in the middle of July. Someone said something nice about the Browns, so we're allowed to smile a little about it.

Meanwhile, there's endless discussion about the Browns quarterback situation, with the latest being NFL.com's Tom Pelissero noting that the quarterback horse race will be "interesting", and saying that Watson will only be tested when he steps onto the field, while being heckled by his team's own fans, and the game speeding up around him. We've seen that particular movie before, and the third or fourth sequel is rarely better than the original, which wasn't well-reviewed, either.

Meanwhile, over in the forums, the fanbase has already moved on from mourning Ethan Pocic's exit to mocking his new employer — the Watercooler thread on his signing is titled, with real affection, "Ethan Pocic Signs with Ratbirds." Ah, yes, nothing the Rats can do isn't noted with scorn. From surfing over social media, it appears there's a big gap between how Ravens fans feel about the acquisition and what the rest of the league thinks (which is not much).

Meanwhile, because the real world is boring, I at least have some interest in way-too-early 2027 mock drafts, if only to quickly scan them and see which quarterback the Browns wind up with. It's generally not Dante Moore or Arch Manning because the Browns are perceived to be just too darn good for the season to tank that badly. So, PFSN has them picking seventh and landing Edge Dylan Stewart to torment future opponents, and then drafting quarterback CJ Carr from Notre Dame with the last pick in the first round, as it's universally agreed that the Rams will win the Super Bowl these days.

So, there are a bunch of people saying things about the Browns based on what may or may not be good analysis, and my comments on them. I feel a little like an aggregator this morning, and it's icky.

I was going to go completely off-topic today and talk about how my approach to managing the OBR has changed over the years, but figured even these third-party takes are more interesting than that. Suffice it to say that the short version of that story is that the OBR has changed from an always-fun hobby to a generally fun, full-time job that sometimes requires me to make uncomfortable decisions. Maybe some other time on that one.

In the meantime, I'm planning to work on my project most of the day, then go outside, light a fire, and burn some sort of meat into oblivion. I hope you enjoy your Sunday as well, and that these bloviations have actual news to respond to in the near future.

Have a good one! GO BROWNS!

text:
During a recent appearance on Sports Radio 810, retired Pro Bowl quarterback Derek Carr shared his thoughts on Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes needing protection in the pocket from his offensive line.

"It's the hardest position in sports. It's the most valuable position in any sport, and you played it at the highest level, and then you watch him. What do you think, knowing everything that goes into playing that position? My hope for him is that they (the Chiefs) take care of him. As good as he is, we all know the talent. We know the Super Bowls," said Carr. "He and Andy (Reid) have won, and all those things, but you see what happens. It's hard to get the job done when we're scrambling or on our backs. If you give Pat (Patrick Mahomes) any time, with a run game and some play action. In every clip I've seen of the Chiefs so far, he's been under center, handing off, and I'm like, yes. I'm telling you, you give him time and protection like that, he's unbelievable."

Carr, a multiple-time Pro Bowler in his playing days, was plagued by injuries late in his career. He understands the value in solid protection from the offensive line and a consistent running game, but sees the special qualities of Mahomes.

Advertisement

"He's accurate. He throws from three-quarters. He throws from over the top sidearm. He can no-look. He can do all those things because he's learned coverage over the years. His mind is growing because he works at it, and so, as you saw at the beginning, we saw this wrong talent, right? You see these crazy plays, and you're like, "Don't do it! Oh, good throw! Oh my gosh, that was amazing! You know, all those things," said Carr. "I think what's scary for the NFL is that he's getting smarter and learning. My thing is when I watch the Chiefs, and I can say this because they can be mad at me all they want. It's like you've got to protect. If you protect, you should be in the AFC Championship fight and go to the Super Bowl every year."

Mahomes finished the 2025 season with 22 touchdown passes and 11 interceptions in 14 games before the knee injury. He also rushed for 422 yards and five touchdowns.

text:
New York Giants fans might be flipping out over what they saw on Saturday.

Budding running back Cam Skattebo had his 2025 rookie season cut short by a devastating ankle injury. The Arizona State product was a bright spot on an otherwise dismal Giants team, with 401 rushing yards on 100 carries (4.1 yards per carry) in limited action.

While Skattebo has been transparent with his injury, recovery and rehab, the running back again showcased the health of his ankle with a backflip gone awry during Fanatics Fest this weekend.

The Giants running back took the stage a WWE event at the convention, showed off the surgically repaired ankle and proceeded to execute a nearly flawless backflip. Instead of landing securely on his feet, however, Skattebo fell, but would jump back up quickly. The East Rutherford judges might give it a 5.

On Sunday, Skattebo wanted to ease the minds of fans, making a guarantee that they will see him on the turf come the start of the season.

"I'm gonna address the elephant: I will not hurt myself before the season," he said, before continuing to explain what went wrong on the backflip.

"When I took off, I was mid-air like, 'holy cow, I'm not gonna land this, I'm way too high,'" he said. "Landed, but it had too much cushion. It wasn't a stiff, firm ground. ...

"Nothing came out from that, I'm perfectly fine. Nothing happened. We're good."

It's not the first time that Skattebo has backflipped this offseason. Another public attempt happened at teammate Brian Burns' celebrity softball game in May after hitting a home run.

The Giants are hoping he hits a lot more home runs for them, this time on the field, in 2026. With new head coach John Harbaugh's reputation of installing bruising, run-first offenses, a healthy Skattebo is expected to factor into that equation.

Cam Skattebo injury update

The Giants running back is expected to be ready for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel expressed confidence in the group during minicamp, declining to put them in the category of a group that needed addition. Landry got off to a hot start in 2025, but a midseason injury limited him down the stretch and into the playoffs. His status to open training camp, along with Jacas', will be something to monitor, with a stint on PUP a possibility after offseason surgery.

Perhaps Landry and Jacas are back and ready to go for the start of the season. Until then, it's a spot where the current depth will get plenty of chances to step up.

Veteran Dre'Mont Jones adds a needed level of security, regardless of Landry's status, and he's a player that is in a similar mold, an every-down edge. The Patriots locked Jones up as their only multi-year signing of free agency on defense, and for good reason, they'll need to rely on the veteran who had seven sacks last season, splitting time between the Titans and Chargers.

Second-year player Elijah Ponder was the first man up this offseason with Landy out after showing solid growth as an undrafted rookie who earned a roster spot, then made growing contributions that included four sacks, two fumble recoveries and 99 snaps in the postseason. Ponder could have a breakout opportunity this season.

Jacas figures to be prominently involved in the edge rotation but was missing from minicamp practices as his injury and contract status remain uncertain. Jacas has the potential to be an all-around edge like Landry and Jones, and plays with the kind of effort and finish that made him an exciting addition to the Patriots defense. Jacas' arrival on the field is one of the key plotlines to start training camp.

Bradyn Swinson saw some expanded opportunities this spring and has pass-rush potential, while free agent signing Jesse Luketa has 31 NFL games played with the Cardinals, including three sacks in 2024.

Amari Gainer is in the mix and has 17 NFL games played for Las Vegas in 2024. He joined the Patriots practice squad in December 2025, experience that could help him put it all together this summer.

Rookies Quintayvious Hutchins (7th-round selection) and Xavier Holmes (UDFA) round out the group, with both having local roots to Boston College and the University of Maine, respectively.

Bottom Line: The first big question of training camp: Are Landry/Jacas PUP'd? Limited? Full go? Their availability will set the ceiling for this group that has a wide variance without them. Jones is a rock-solid pro, and Ponder has real potential, but they are not enough on their own. That could set up an interesting depth battle between Swinson, Luketa, Gainer and the rookies in August. Once everyone is back in the mix the big question is, does this group have the juice off the edge to open things up inside for Williams and Barmore? This position group has 'make-or-break' potential for a defense with Super Bowl aspirations.

For some football players, the attitude that makes them great on the field can tempt them to do dumb things off the field.

Case in point: Giants running back Cam Skattebo.

In November, not long after he suffered a season-ending ankle injury, he was pushing and shoving at a WWE event. Now that his ankle has healed, Skattebo wanted to prove it during an appearance at Fanatics Fest.

After pulling up the leg of his pants to expose the ankle that had been dislocated (along with a tibia fracture), Skattebo did a backflip. He didn’t stick the landing.

Skattebo stumbled backward and fell, before springing up and acting like he meant to do that.

As many have suggested, Giants coach John Harbaugh may not be thrilled when he sees the video. And while some have pointed out that Harbaugh once yelled at quarterback Joe Flacco for riding a skateboard during the playoff run that resulted in a Ravens Super Bowl win, it wasn’t Harbaugh — it was former G.M. Ozzie Newsome.

Regardless, it’s a valid concern. Even if Skattebo will eventually be taking much greater risks with his health when it’s time to get hit and tackled, there’s no reason to add to the risks by doing other things that could result in an injury.

title: Bukayo Saka needs managing, but proved again he is vital to England and Arsenal's key moments
description:
Arsenal and England fans could have been forgiven for raising eyebrows when they saw Thomas Tuchel’s England starting XI for the World Cup third-placed play-off against France.
He was ready to go in the World Cup.
At the 2022 World Cup and 2024 European Championship, the debate was over whether Phil Foden or Saka should start on the right.
Before this month’s semi-final, Saka became just the third English player to assist three goals at a World Cup, averaging one every 64 minutes.
Kane could play at 34 in the next Euros in 2028, but having an equally integral role at 36 at the 2030 World Cup seems unlikely.
text:
Arsenal and England fans could have been forgiven for raising eyebrows when they saw Thomas Tuchel’s England starting XI for the World Cup third-placed play-off against France.

Declan Rice’s inclusion may have increased heart rates given the hamstring issues he has been nursing, but Bukayo Saka starting and scoring a hat-trick while completing 90 minutes just days after not being brought on in the semi-final defeat to Argentina begged the question, “Why now?” for many.

In fairness to Saka, when asked by BBC Sport if he could have played a bigger part in England’s tournament, what else would he say other than: “Of course I would have loved to have played more, but it’s too late to talk about that. I try to do my talking on the pitch.” He added “I’m fit” when pushed.

In the semi-final, Tuchel spoke of Morgan Rogers’ physicality as a reason to start, and then about the crazy nature of the second half when opting for different substitutions rather than bringing on Saka.

The German added: “Bukayo is a key player. He was ready to go in the World Cup. I still felt the responsibility as a coach and with the (injury) history he came from, to take it slow with Bukayo. He started some matches and it was a tough decision to leave him out of the semi-final.”

Saka could not train early in the World Cup because of his recent Achilles issue and Tuchel’s comments came in the context of the 24-year-old going full pelt for club and country since his teens — Saka ranked in the top two for minutes played at Arsenal for three successive seasons between the ages of 18 and 21.

The issue most may struggle to get past is not that Saka did not start against Argentina, but that he did not come on at all.

His response on the pitch in the display against France may feed result-based conclusions, but his history with England should give an indication of how critical he is to their present and future.

Saka has constantly stepped up for England at tournaments despite questions over him.

He came into Euro 2020 with some insisting he should be used as a left wing-back, but stole the show at right wing in the round-of-16 win over Germany and took a penalty in the shootout defeat to Italy in the final aged 19. At the 2022 World Cup and 2024 European Championship, the debate was over whether Phil Foden or Saka should start on the right.

Saka got the nod, and responded with important moments, including a penalty-winning foul against France in the 2022 quarter-finals, an assist for England’s only goal in their opening win over Serbia in 2024 and a late equaliser against Switzerland later in the tournament.

Before this month’s semi-final, Saka became just the third English player to assist three goals at a World Cup, averaging one every 64 minutes. These too were important, with the openers against Panama and Mexico assisted by him and scored by Jude Bellingham.

These two players are the most reliable attacking figures England will have in a post-Harry Kane world. Saka was the third top-scorer for England in this summer’s World Cup squad before the tournament began, behind Kane (aged 32) and Marcus Rashford (aged 28). Kane could play at 34 in the next Euros in 2028, but having an equally integral role at 36 at the 2030 World Cup seems unlikely.

With these tournaments in mind, the responsibility felt by Tuchel this summer and Mikel Arteta towards the back end of the season (when Saka’s minutes were managed with Arsenal) becomes even more important. Arteta cited the impact of accumulated game time across seasons, specifically in relation to Saka, days after he tore a hamstring in December 2024, and did look to rotate more on the right wing with the signing of Noni Madueke last season.

Neither Arteta nor Tuchel will want to be in situations where they cannot use one of the most influential players in their biggest games, so continuing to protect him could be vital in upcoming seasons and tournaments.

Comparisons were made between how Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain use players before this year’s Champions League final, with nine Arsenal players playing more than 2,000 league minutes compared with PSG’s three.

While the strength of the Premier League compared with Ligue 1 makes rotation more difficult, the demands on Saka have been non-stop since he arrived in the first team.

Saka will get at least three weeks off now, but the demands of a new season should not override a clear need to be eased back in, even if the winger says he is fit.

He featured in both of Arsenal’s opening league matches after helping England reach the final of the last two European Championships. The weight of three points in the Premier League contributed to that, but looking ahead to the 2026-27 season and beyond, more long-term thinking would benefit the futures of Saka, Arsenal and England.

He will deliver when called upon — it is just a matter of enabling him to answer the call in the best way possible.
